speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me. To help narrow down the cause of your wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions, can you describe the appearance and location of the skin lesions in detail? Also, do you recall any recent insect bites or exposure to animals?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your recent camping trip in Minnesota and the self-resolving knee pain, were the skin lesions accompanied by a fever at the time, and do you recall any specific insect bites or exposure to ticks or mosquitoes?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology photos of the lesions and left wrist X-ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL. ESR: Normal. CRP: Normal. Dermatology images: Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions noted on the dorsum of both wrists and hands; two lesions on the left palm. Left wrist X-ray: Normal.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.
